title: Consumers, acks and prefetch
summary: Manual acks, nack and reject, requeue and the redelivered flag, prefetch and competing consumers: how RabbitMQ hands out messages and gets them back.

steps.title: The life of a delivery
body: A queue holds **ready** messages. When it delivers one to a consumer, the message becomes **unacked**: still
in the queue, invisible to others, waiting for the consumer's verdict.
```text
ready ──deliver (delivery tag 1, 2, 3 ... per channel)──> unacked ──┬─ ack ───────────────────> removed
^                                                                ├─ nack/reject requeue=true ─┐
│                                                                ├─ nack/reject requeue=false ──> dead-letter exchange (or dropped)
│                                                                └─ channel or connection closes ┐
- With **`autoAck: true`** the broker forgets the message the moment it sends it: *at most once*. A consumer
crash loses everything it had received.
- With manual acks, a crash or a closed channel requeues the unacked messages: *at least once*, so duplicates
are possible and consumers must be idempotent.
- A delivery not acked within `consumer_timeout` (30 minutes by default) closes the channel and requeues it.
> **See it:** **Labs → Messaging builder → RabbitMQ**, challenge *Auto-ack ate my order*.

steps.prompt: A consumer runs with `autoAck: true` and a prefetch of 20. It has received 20 messages and finished 3 when the pod is killed. What happens to the other 17?
options: They are lost: the broker removed them when it delivered them
They go to the dead-letter exchange
They stay unacked until the consumer comes back
steps.explain: Auto-ack is fire-and-forget delivery. Use it only for data you can afford to lose (metrics samples); business messages need manual acks after the work is done.

steps.title: A consumer with RabbitMQ.Client 7
body: ```csharp fragment
await channel.BasicQosAsync(prefetchSize: 0, prefetchCount: 20, global: false);
var consumer = new AsyncEventingBasicConsumer(channel);
consumer.ReceivedAsync += async (_, ea) =>
try
var order = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Order>(ea.Body.Span)!;
await billing.ChargeAsync(order, ea.BasicProperties.MessageId);
await channel.BasicAckAsync(ea.DeliveryTag, multiple: false);
catch (JsonException)
await channel.BasicNackAsync(ea.DeliveryTag, multiple: false, requeue: false);  // poison: to the DLX
catch (TimeoutException) when (!ea.Redelivered)
await channel.BasicNackAsync(ea.DeliveryTag, multiple: false, requeue: true);   // one quick second chance
await channel.BasicConsumeAsync("billing", autoAck: false, consumer: consumer);
- Ack or nack on the **same channel** that received the message; delivery tags are per channel.
- `multiple: true` acks every tag up to this one in one frame. `BasicRejectAsync` is nack for one message.
- `Redelivered` means "**may** have been delivered before", not a count. Quorum queues add an
`x-delivery-count` header when you need the number.
- An exception that escapes the handler leaves the message **unacked** until the channel closes. Every path
must end in an ack or a nack.
> **Older code:** 6.x used `EventingBasicConsumer` with a synchronous `Received` event and `channel.BasicAck(...)`.

steps.prompt: A worker runs report jobs that take minutes each. Each worker should hold **one job at a time**, a broken message must go to the dead-letter exchange, and a worker crash must not lose a job. Fill the gaps.
steps.explain: Prefetch 1 for long jobs, so a busy worker does not sit on jobs another could start. `requeue: false` sends the poison message to the DLX instead of straight back to the queue. `autoAck: false` keeps the job in the queue until it is done.

steps.title: Prefetch: how many unacked messages per consumer
body: `BasicQosAsync(0, prefetchCount, false)` caps how many **unacked** messages each consumer on the channel may
hold. The queue hands messages round-robin to consumers that have a free slot.
- **Prefetch 0 means unlimited**: the first consumer to connect gets the whole backlog, the others get nothing,
and its memory fills up (*One greedy consumer*).
- **Too low** for fast messages: every message waits for an ack round-trip, throughput drops.
- Rule of thumb: 10 to 50 for short handlers, **1** for long jobs, then measure.
Step through two consumers with prefetch 2: `fast` acks everything it holds each round, `slow` never does.
The slow consumer keeps its two messages; the fast one takes all the rest.
> **See it:** **Labs → Messaging builder → RabbitMQ**, challenge *One greedy consumer*.

code: var unacked = new Dictionary<string, List<string>> { ["fast"] = new(), ["slow"] = new() };
if (ready.Count > 0 && unacked[c].Count < prefetch) { unacked[c].Add(ready.Dequeue()); gave = true; }

prompt: **Symptom first.** Three report workers run, but only `worker-a` is busy (100 % CPU, 3 GB of memory and
climbing); the other two are idle. What is the cause and the fix?
code: $ rabbitmqctl list_queues name messages_ready messages_unacknowledged consumers
$ rabbitmqctl list_consumers queue_name consumer_tag ack_required prefetch_count
options: Prefetch 0 means unlimited: worker-a connected first and took all 4,800 messages. Call `BasicQosAsync(0, 1, false)` before consuming and restart the workers.
`ack_required = true` means acknowledgements are switched off; set it to false.
Three consumers on one queue is too many; give each worker its own queue.
worker-b and worker-c use the wrong routing key.
explain: `messages_unacknowledged = 4800` with `messages_ready = 0` says every message is in flight, and
`prefetch_count = 0` says nothing limited it. Once the greedy worker restarts, its unacked messages are
requeued and spread over all three.

steps.prompt: What should the consumer do with each delivery?
items: Saved to the database and published the follow-up event
Already processed this `MessageId` (found in the inbox table)
The body is not valid JSON
The service is shutting down and has not started the work
The same message hit a deadlock again, `Redelivered = true`
steps.explain: Ack what is done (including duplicates you skip). Requeue only when another try right now has a real chance. Anything that will fail again goes to the DLX, or it loops forever (lesson 4 and module 6).

steps.title: Ack, requeue or dead-letter?
prompt: Write `string Decide(string outcome, bool redelivered)` returning `"ack"`, `"requeue"` or `"dead-letter"`:
| `outcome` | decision |
| `"ok"`, `"duplicate"` | `"ack"` |
| `"permanent"` | `"dead-letter"` |
| `"transient"` | `"requeue"` the first time, `"dead-letter"` when `redelivered` |
| `"shutdown"` | `"requeue"` (the work never started; not the message's fault) |
Any other outcome throws `ArgumentException`.
solution: string Decide(string outcome, bool redelivered) => outcome switch
hints: A `switch` expression with `"ok" or "duplicate" => "ack"` reads well.
template: Dojo.Eq("a duplicate is acked, not retried", "ack", Decide("duplicate", true));
Dojo.Eq("permanent goes to the DLX", "dead-letter", Decide("permanent", false));
Dojo.Eq("transient, first delivery: requeue", "requeue", Decide("transient", false));

steps.title: A queue with prefetch, acks and requeue
prompt: Model a RabbitMQ queue and its consumers. Write a class `BrokerQueue`:
- `BrokerQueue(int prefetch)`: the per-consumer limit of unacked messages; `0` means unlimited.
- `void Publish(string message)`: adds to the end of the ready list.
- `void AddConsumer(string name)`: consumers are served in the order they were added.
- `List<string> Dispatch()`: hands out ready messages one at a time, round-robin over the consumers that have
a free slot (each pass starts with the first consumer), until nothing is ready or nobody has room. Each
delivery gets the consumer's next **delivery tag** (`1`, `2`, ... per consumer) and is reported as
`"{consumer} #{tag} {message}"`, plus `" (redelivered)"` if it was delivered before.
- `void Ack(string consumer, ulong tag, bool multiple = false)`: removes that unacked delivery; with
`multiple`, every unacked delivery of that consumer with a tag up to `tag`. A tag that is not unacked (or an
unknown consumer) throws `InvalidOperationException`, like the broker's `PRECONDITION_FAILED - unknown delivery tag`.
- `void Nack(string consumer, ulong tag, bool requeue)`: `requeue` puts the message back at the **front** of
the ready list, marked redelivered; otherwise it goes to `DeadLetters`. Unknown tags throw as for `Ack`.
- `void Disconnect(string consumer)`: removes the consumer; its unacked messages go back to the front of the
ready list in tag order, marked redelivered.
- `int Ready`, `int Unacked`, `List<string> DeadLetters` (get-only).
starter: public void Ack(string consumer, ulong tag, bool multiple = false) { }
public void Nack(string consumer, ulong tag, bool requeue) { }
solution: public List<(ulong Tag, string Message)> Unacked = new();
readonly List<(string Message, bool Redelivered)> ready = new();
public void Publish(string message) => ready.Add((message, false));
public void Ack(string consumer, ulong tag, bool multiple = false)
var removed = c.Unacked.RemoveAll(u => multiple ? u.Tag <= tag : u.Tag == tag);
if (removed == 0) throw new InvalidOperationException($"PRECONDITION_FAILED - unknown delivery tag {tag}");
public void Nack(string consumer, ulong tag, bool requeue)
if (i < 0) throw new InvalidOperationException($"PRECONDITION_FAILED - unknown delivery tag {tag}");
consumers.TryGetValue(name, out var c) ? c : throw new InvalidOperationException($"unknown consumer '{name}'");
hints: Keep the ready list as `List<(string Message, bool Redelivered)>` so requeues can go to index 0.
Per consumer: a tag counter and a list of `(ulong Tag, string Message)` unacked deliveries.
`Dispatch`: repeat passes over the consumers while at least one message was handed out in the pass.
template: Dojo.Eq("round-robin up to prefetch 2", new List<string> { "c1 #1 m1", "c2 #1 m2", "c1 #2 m3", "c2 #2 m4" }, dojoQ.Dispatch());
Dojo.Eq("multiple ack frees both of c1's slots", 2, dojoQ.Unacked);
Dojo.Eq("c1 gets the last one", new List<string> { "c1 #3 m5" }, dojoQ.Dispatch());
Dojo.Eq("requeued message comes back first, marked", new List<string> { "c1 #4 m2 (redelivered)" }, dojoQ.Dispatch());
Dojo.Eq("nack without requeue dead-letters", new List<string> { "m4" }, dojoQ.DeadLetters);
Dojo.Eq("a disconnect requeues unacked in tag order", 2, dojoQ.Ready);
Dojo.Eq("the other consumer gets them", new List<string> { "c2 #3 m5 (redelivered)", "c2 #4 m2 (redelivered)" }, dojoQ.Dispatch());
Dojo.Eq("prefetch 0: the first consumer takes everything", 5, dojoG.Dispatch().Count);
Dojo.Eq("the late consumer gets nothing", 0, dojoG.Dispatch().Count);
